muuga_centre_location.title: Location & Route

directions.title: On foot: about 20 minutes (1.8 km)
directions.sub: From Gate 1, follow the pavement along Nuudi tee to the junction with Altmetsa tee, then turn right

muuga_centre_location.note: At night the road is poorly lit with heavy truck traffic — wear a hi-vis vest and a reflector, and consider the shuttle instead of walking after dark.

muuga_transport_taxi.title: Taxi

rows.title: Bolt
rows.sub: Set pickup to "Muuga Sadam Peavärav / Gate 1"

rows.title: Uber
rows.sub: Also available

rows.title: The car park in front of Gate 1
rows.sub: Taxis don't enter the secured zone without a special pass

muuga_transport_taxi.note: €18–25 into central Tallinn; €5–7 to the nearby town of Maardu. Street pickups are rare out here simply because of the distance — always order through an app rather than expecting to flag one down, and never try to call a taxi right to the ship's side, security won't let it through.

muuga_transport_public.note: About 35–45 minutes to central Tallinn. Last bus 34 runs around 23:00. No in-port shuttle for getting from the ship to the gate itself — that's arranged by your agent or the Seamen's Mission, free of charge, by request.

callout.text: Never exchange money on the street, even for a good rate someone offers you. In some countries this is a criminal offence — and it's one of the most common ways seafarers get scammed near a port.

rows.title: A stranger offers you a better rate
rows.sub: On the street, at the gate, or "just around the corner" — always a scam

rows.title: Being asked to go somewhere private
rows.sub: A car, a back room, an alley — a legitimate exchange never needs this

rows.title: No receipt offered
rows.sub: A real exchange always gives you a printed receipt with the rate used

rows.title: Know the rough official rate first
rows.sub: Check on your phone before you go — so you can spot a bad deal immediately

rows.title: Count what you receive, before you walk away
rows.sub: In front of the person who gave it to you, not after

muuga_city_culture.title: Culture & Must-See

rows.title: Seamen's Centre itself
rows.sub: 1.8 km from the gate — pool table, Wi-Fi, a place to unwind

rows.title: Maardu town
rows.sub: 5 km — small and pleasant, a park, an Orthodox church, squares

rows.title: Lasnamäe Centrum mall, Tallinn
rows.sub: 12 km — for shopping

rows.title: Tallinn Old Town
rows.sub: 18 km — only worth it with a taxi/bus and at least 4–5 hours to spare

muuga_city_culture.note: Muuga is genuinely a working port, well outside the city — the Old Town is a real excursion from here, not a quick walk like at Vanasadam. Plan your time accordingly.

muuga_city_free.title: Free Time & Relax

rows.title: Muuga Seamen's Centre
rows.sub: By far the best option — sockets, sofas, free Wi-Fi, hot tea, and it's safe

muuga_city_free.note: Out here, the centre isn't just one option among several — it's genuinely the place to be. Everything else involves a real trip.

callout.text: Before you leave, agree your return time with the ship and mark your ship's position on the Ship screen. Getting back to the right berth after dark, across a working industrial port, is a real risk here — take it seriously.
